attrs.evidence: GPT-5.6's MOS-CANONICAL-VIEWS proposes: 'if a view can be regenerated from canonical records, make regeneration the invariant.' AS WORDED IT WOULD NOT CATCH THE DRIFT ALREADY LIVE IN THIS TREE. `opensentience.org/box-and-box/` is a manual copy of `AmpersandBoxDesign/box-and-box/` and nothing syncs it; the playground page imports the served copy, so a kernel change is invisible there until three files are copied across by hand. That copy COULD be regenerated at every moment it was wrong — regenerability held continuously while the view was stale. The invariant has to be the comparison, run by a gate that fails. Implemented for one view: mosaic/derived/occupancy.json is regenerated from the shipped table plus the occupancy rules, and scripts/check-mosaic.mjs recomputes and diffs it.
attrs.gap: ONE view is registered. The box-and-box copy that motivated the record is NOT brought under the mechanism this round — it is another lane's file and a parallel session has been editing that tree.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6 (Mosaic audit §3) for the canonical/derived distinction, which is the right question. The strengthening is this round's and its seed incident is live rather than historical.
attrs.statement: A derived view declares its generator and its named inputs, and the gate RECOMPUTES it and compares. Regenerability is not the invariant; equality with the regeneration is.
